# Leave-one-out cross-validation

Estimate how well a fit predicts each observation when that observation
is left out, by Pareto-smoothed importance-sampling leave-one-out
cross-validation (PSIS-LOO; Vehtari et al. 2017).

## Usage

``` r
# S3 method for class 'kb_fit'
loo(x, ...)
```

## Arguments

- x:

  A `kb_fit` object.

- ...:

  Passed to [`loo::loo()`](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/loo.html),
  for example `cores`.

## Value

A `psis_loo` object from
[`loo::loo()`](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/loo.html).

## Details

The pointwise results (`$pointwise` and
[`loo::pareto_k_values()`](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/pareto-k-diagnostic.html))
have one row per observation, in the order of the fitted data.
`elpd_loo` and the Pareto k diagnostic are described in
[`kb_influence()`](https://hakaiinstitute.github.io/kelpbio/reference/kb_influence.md),
which adds them to the data. A Pareto k above the threshold in the
printed result also marks the PSIS-LOO estimate as unreliable.

Use
[`loo::loo_compare()`](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/loo_compare.html)
to compare fits to the same data.

## References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., and Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model
evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and
Computing, 27, 1413-1432.

## See also

[`log_lik()`](https://mc-stan.org/rstantools/reference/log_lik.html) for
the pointwise log-likelihood.

Other diagnostics:
[`kb_converged()`](https://hakaiinstitute.github.io/kelpbio/reference/kb_converged.md),
[`kb_influence()`](https://hakaiinstitute.github.io/kelpbio/reference/kb_influence.md),
[`kb_plot_trace()`](https://hakaiinstitute.github.io/kelpbio/reference/kb_plot_trace.md),
[`kb_sensitivity()`](https://hakaiinstitute.github.io/kelpbio/reference/kb_sensitivity.md),
[`pp_check.kb_fit()`](https://hakaiinstitute.github.io/kelpbio/reference/pp_check.kb_fit.md)

## Examples

``` r
loo_weight <- loo(fit_weight_sim_nereo)
loo_weight
#> 
#> Computed from 1500 by 660 log-likelihood matrix.
#> 
#>          Estimate   SE
#> elpd_loo   -242.5 32.5
#> p_loo        30.3  1.8
#> looic       485.0 65.1
#> ------
#> MCSE of elpd_loo is 0.2.
#> MCSE and ESS estimates assume MCMC draws (r_eff in [0.7, 1.2]).
#> 
#> All Pareto k estimates are good (k < 0.69).
#> See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
loo::pareto_k_values(loo_weight)
```
